repository.name: @webex/plugin-authorization-browser
repository.purpose: Browser authorization plugin registered as webex.authorization for the public browser build (re-exported by the @webex/plugin-authorization browser entry). It starts OAuth implicit-grant (public client, default) or authorization-code (confidential client) logins with a single-use CSRF token, parses an implicit-grant access token from the redirect URL hash during construction (CSRF check, URL scrubbing, next-tick hand-off to credentials), exchanges a host JWT for an access token through hydra jwt/login, mints HS256 guest JWTs, and redirects on logout. It does not exchange authorization codes.

authorization-browser-sdk.summary: Published npm package. main is dist/index.js and devMain is src/index.js. Importing it imports @webex/internal-plugin-device and registers Authorization as public plugin 'authorization' with proxies isAuthorizing and isAuthenticating and the credentials config default clientType 'public' from src/config.js; the first registration of the name wins. Exports are the default Authorization class and the named config. The plugin API on webex.authorization is initiateLogin, initiateImplicitGrant, initiateAuthorizationCodeGrant, requestAccessTokenFromJwt, createJwt, and logout, plus the ready, isAuthorizing, and isAuthenticating properties. Per-method behavior is in src/docs/README.md.

idbroker-oauth-pages.source: Identity broker authorize and logout pages (URLs from webex-core credentials config; route definitions are not in this repository)
idbroker-oauth-pages.summary: Reached only by browser navigation to URLs built by credentials buildLoginUrl ({response_type token or code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, base64url state with csrf_token, and other options}) and buildLogoutUrl ({cisService, goto, token, and other options}). The implicit-grant redirect returns access_token, token_type, expires_in, optional refresh_token and refresh_token_expires_in, and state in the URL hash; an OAuth error returns in the query.

hydra-jwt-login.source: Hydra jwt/login (reached as service name 'hydra' through the services catalog, else HYDRA_SERVICE_URL, else https://api.ciscospark.com/v1/; route definitions are not in this repository)
hydra-jwt-login.summary: POST <hydra>jwt/login with the JWT in the authorization header returns {token, expiresIn}, mapped to a Bearer supertoken.

webex-core-plugin-host.summary: Authorization extends WebexPlugin in namespace Credentials, is registered with registerPlugin (first-wins, proxies supported), sends requests with this.webex.request, reads this.webex.getWindow(), and is called by WebexCore#logout with token defaulted from the supertoken.

webex-core-credentials.summary: buildLoginUrl and buildLogoutUrl build URLs; credentials.set({supertoken}) stores tokens; grantErrors.select maps OAuth error strings; in JWT mode refresh() calls jwtRefreshCallback and then this plugin's requestAccessTokenFromJwt.

webex-core-services.summary: get('hydra', true) supplies the hydra URL; initServiceCatalogs() runs after a JWT exchange.

webex-common-utilities.summary: base64 (base64url) decodes and encodes the OAuth state in the hash; oneFlight decorates requestAccessTokenFromJwt; whileInFlight decorates initiateImplicitGrant and initiateAuthorizationCodeGrant.

internal-plugin-device-registration.summary: Imported by src/index.js only for its side effect of registering internal plugin 'device' and its onBeforeLogout unregister hook.

jsonwebtoken.summary: jwt.sign(payload, secret, {expiresIn}) produces the HS256 guest JWT; an undefined expiresIn option is rejected.

uuid.summary: uuid.v4 generates the CSRF token; the default export generates the guest subject and default display name.

lodash.summary: cloneDeep, isEmpty, and omit for hash parsing and URL cleanup.
